references.text: Repeats the prohibition against sacrificing outside the tabernacle and elaborates on the consequences for anyone who breaks this command.
Permits slaughtering animals for food outside the sanctuary, but distinguishes between ordinary slaughter and sacrifice.
Grants permission to slaughter animals at home when the distance to the sanctuary is great.
Describes that the burnt offering of cattle must be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting, showing the correct sacrificial practice.
Mentions the peace offering of cattle and how it should be presented before the Lord at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Instructs that whoever brings a peace offering must personally bring their gift to the Lord at the sanctuary.
Shows that oxen must be slaughtered in the presence of the Lord at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
